checks.rule: A legal boundary is an exact line with no thickness or width.
The exact legal boundary is rarely identified with precision on the ground or in conveyances and transfers.
Ordnance Survey mapping does not itself show the exact legal boundary.
A physical feature such as a fence, wall or hedge may or may not coincide with the legal boundary.
Do not equate a visible physical feature with the legal boundary without supporting title or determined-boundary evidence.
Physical-boundary position recorded on a plan depends on the accuracy and tolerances of the underlying survey.
Large-scale Ordnance Survey mapping is subject to defined survey tolerances.
Legal-boundary position depends on the relevant conveyance or transfer considered as a whole, including its plan.
Where a plan is insufficiently clear, do not fabricate precision; external evidence and historic physical features may be required.
General-boundary registration leaves the exact line undetermined.
Red edging can be adjusted to better show general position without converting the boundary into an exact determined boundary.
Any parcel-height workflow must preserve boundary-position uncertainty separately from elevation uncertainty.
